sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: There are currently more than 31,000 post offices in the United States.
sentences.zh: 目前美国有超过31000个邮局。

sentences.en: There are grand old ones that take up entire city blocks,
sentences.zh: 有占据整个街区的宏伟老建筑，

sentences.en: and there are smaller, humbler ones hiding away in the backs of general stores in towns across rural America.
sentences.zh: 也有隐藏在乡村小店后方、朴实无华的小邮局。

sentences.en: But this one in Arizona may be the most rural post office in the continental U.S.
sentences.zh: 但亚利桑那州的这个邮局，可能是美国本土最偏远的邮局。

sentences.en: The Supai post office is located at the bottom of the Grand Canyon.
sentences.zh: 苏派邮局位于大峡谷底部。

sentences.en: That's Vivian Campbell.
sentences.zh: 那是薇薇安·坎贝尔。

sentences.en: My name is Vivian Campbell, and I am the postmaster of Peach Springs, Arizona.
sentences.zh: 我叫薇薇安·坎贝尔，是亚利桑那州桃泉镇的邮政局长。

sentences.en: Vivian works closely with the Supai post office,
sentences.zh: 薇薇安与苏派邮局紧密合作，

sentences.en: and she says there are only a few ways to get mail to the bottom of the Grand Canyon.
sentences.zh: 她说要把邮件送到大峡谷底部，只有几种方法。

sentences.en: You either have to hike down there, ride a mule, or ride a horse.
sentences.zh: 要么徒步走下去，要么骑骡子，要么骑马。

sentences.en: And so, every day, rain or shine, mail gets packed on 10 mules to make a two-and-a-half-hour trip into the canyon.
sentences.zh: 所以，无论刮风下雨，每天都有邮件装在10头骡子上，开启进入峡谷的两个半小时旅程。

sentences.en: The post office is there to serve the people who live on the Avasupai Reservation.
sentences.zh: 这个邮局是为了服务居住在哈瓦苏派保留地的人们。

sentences.en: Avasupai meaning blue-green water people, named for the waterfall at the bottom of the canyon.
sentences.zh: 哈瓦苏派意为“蓝绿水之民”，得名于峡谷底部的瀑布。

sentences.en: The falls are just magnificent.
sentences.zh: 那里的瀑布简直壮观极了。

sentences.en: The water is so blue, it's not even, it's indescribable.
sentences.zh: 水蓝得甚至无法用语言形容。

sentences.en: The Avasupai receive a lot of food supplies, but otherwise their mail is pretty standard fare.
sentences.zh: 哈瓦苏派人会收到许多食品补给，除此之外，他们的邮件大多是普通信件。

sentences.en: They get packages from Amazon, they get first-class mail, they get bills just like you and me.
sentences.zh: 他们像你我一样，会收到亚马逊的包裹、一类邮件和账单。

sentences.en: The Supai post office was established in 1896,
sentences.zh: 苏派邮局成立于1896年，

sentences.en: and its existence speaks to the lengths that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 它的存在证明了美国邮政为了连接人们，

sentences.en: post office has gone to connect people with each other
sentences.zh: 以及自18世纪末邮政服务创立以来，

sentences.en: and to unite us as a country, ever since the service was founded in the late 1700s.
sentences.zh: 为了将我们团结为一个国家所付出的努力。

sentences.en: I was sitting on my back porch in Wyoming one night, you know, as the sun sank in the Golden West,
sentences.zh: 有一天晚上，我坐在怀俄明州的后廊上，看着太阳沉入金色的西部，

sentences.en: and I just jumped up out of the chair and like shrieked at my husband.
sentences.zh: 我突然从椅子上跳起来，对我丈夫尖叫道：

sentences.en: The post office created America.
sentences.zh: “邮政系统创造了美国。”

sentences.en: That is author and historian Winifred Gallagher,
sentences.zh: 那是作家兼历史学家温妮弗雷德·加拉格尔，

sentences.en: and she wrote a book based on this revelation called, appropriately,
sentences.zh: 她根据这一发现写了一本书，书名非常贴切，

sentences.en: How the Post Office Created America, a History.
sentences.zh: 叫《邮政如何创造了美国：一部历史》。

sentences.en: Gallagher argues that the post office didn't just create an efficient and inexpensive way
sentences.zh: 加拉格尔认为，邮政系统不仅创造了一种高效且廉价的方式，

sentences.en: to send a letter from Oakland, California into the Grand Canyon.
sentences.zh: 能把信件从加州奥克兰寄到大峡谷，

sentences.en: The service was designed to unite a bunch of disparate towns and people under one flag.
sentences.zh: 这项服务旨在将一群分散的城镇和人民团结在同一面旗帜下。

sentences.en: And in doing so, the post office actually created the United States of America.
sentences.zh: 通过这种方式，邮政系统实际上创造了美利坚合众国。

sentences.en: For thousands of years, governments have had ways of sending information across distances.
sentences.zh: 几千年来，各国政府都有跨距离传递信息的方法。

sentences.en: But for most of history, the mail was limited to correspondence between governments,
sentences.zh: 但在历史上大部分时间里，邮件仅限于政府、

sentences.en: militaries, and eventually, wealthy people who could afford to pay for such a service.
sentences.zh: 军队，以及后来那些付得起钱的富人之间的通信。

sentences.en: And that's what the postal system of early colonized America was like.
sentences.zh: 早期的殖民地美国邮政系统就是这样。

sentences.en: The Crown's post was put in place by the English monarchy
sentences.zh: 英国皇室设立了皇家邮政，

sentences.en: and was mostly used to get messages from England to America.
sentences.zh: 主要用于将信息从英国传送到美国。

sentences.en: Once the mail landed from England into America,
sentences.zh: 一旦邮件从英国抵达美国，

sentences.en: it would be circulated by a fellow called a post rider who, just like he sounds, he was a man on a horse.
sentences.zh: 就会由一名所谓的“邮差”分发，正如其名，他就是骑马送信的人。

sentences.en: There were no roads suitable for a wheeled vehicle.
sentences.zh: 当时没有适合轮式车辆行驶的道路。

sentences.en: At the time, the colonies, which dotted the eastern coast from New Hampshire down to Georgia,
sentences.zh: 那时，从新罕布什尔州到佐治亚州沿东海岸分布的殖民地，

sentences.en: weren't that interested in communicating with each other.
sentences.zh: 对彼此之间的交流并不感兴趣。

sentences.en: The colonies were very fractious, disputatious siblings.
sentences.zh: 殖民地就像一群爱争吵、好辩论的兄弟姐妹。

sentences.en: They had very little to do with each other.
sentences.zh: 他们几乎互不往来。

sentences.en: They were clamoring for the attention of Mother England.
sentences.zh: 他们都在争相博取“母亲”英国的关注。

sentences.en: But all of this started to change when an enterprising fellow named Benjamin Franklin
sentences.zh: 但当一位名叫本杰明·富兰克林的进取之士，

sentences.en: became postmaster for the Crown.
sentences.zh: 成为皇家邮政局长后，这一切开始改变。

sentences.en: As postmaster, Franklin was in charge of making sure mail in the colonies got to its proper location,
sentences.zh: 作为邮政局长，富兰克林负责确保殖民地的邮件能送到正确地点，

sentences.en: and he was determined to improve the bare-bone system.
sentences.zh: 他决心改善这个简陋的系统。

sentences.en: He actually visited every colony.
sentences.zh: 他实际上走访了每一个殖民地。

sentences.en: This was back when it was a real pain in the neck.
sentences.zh: 那是在那个过程非常痛苦的年代。

sentences.en: He established mileposts so you could charge fairly for the distance a letter was going
sentences.zh: 他设立了里程碑，这样就可以根据信件传输的距离公平收费，

sentences.en: instead of just estimating it.
sentences.zh: 而不是仅仅靠估算。

sentences.en: But as Franklin worked to improve the Crown system,
sentences.zh: 但随着富兰克林努力改善皇家邮政系统，

sentences.en: he began to see the colonies differently.
sentences.zh: 他开始以不同的眼光看待这些殖民地。

sentences.en: I believe that the process of going around and thinking about these 13 colonies
sentences.zh: 我相信，通过走访并思考这13个殖民地，

sentences.en: as not just disconnected, but links in a chain,
sentences.zh: 不再把它们看作互不关联的个体，而是链条上的环节，

sentences.en: I think this started him thinking about ways that they could come together as a people.
sentences.zh: 我认为这让他开始思考它们作为一个民族团结起来的方式。

sentences.en: In 1754, at a meeting of colonial representatives in Albany, New York,
sentences.zh: 1754年，在纽约州奥尔巴尼的一次殖民地代表会议上，

sentences.en: Franklin proposed a plan for uniting the colonies.
sentences.zh: 富兰克林提出了统一殖民地的计划。

sentences.en: He actually kind of sketched out a federal government where the colonies would elect their own
sentences.zh: 他实际上勾勒出了一个联邦政府的雏形，由殖民地选举自己的

sentences.en: representatives as opposed to having them appointed by the Crown.
sentences.zh: 代表，而不是由皇室任命。

sentences.en: England didn't appreciate Franklin's ideas, and colonists weren't quite ready for them either.
sentences.zh: 英国不欣赏富兰克林的想法，殖民者也还没准备好接受它们。

sentences.en: But 20 years later, notions about American self-governance were spreading.
sentences.zh: 但20年后，关于美国自治的观念开始传播。

sentences.en: Revolutionaries in the colonies needed a way to communicate about the growing movement
sentences.zh: 殖民地的革命者需要一种方式来交流日益增长的独立运动，

sentences.en: for independence, and they knew they couldn't use the Crown's poSt.
sentences.zh: 他们知道不能使用皇家邮政。

sentences.en: Because if they used the Crown's system, their letters would be intercepted and they'd be arrested.
sentences.zh: 因为如果使用皇家系统，他们的信件会被拦截，他们会被逮捕。

sentences.en: In 1774, these American revolutionaries created their own system to communicate called
sentences.zh: 1774年，这些美国革命者创建了自己的通信系统，称为

sentences.en: the Constitutional PoSt.
sentences.zh: “宪政邮政”。

sentences.en: Before they fought the Revolution, or had a system of government,
sentences.zh: 在他们进行革命或拥有政府体系之前，

sentences.en: before the Declaration of Independence and the Constitution,
sentences.zh: 在《独立宣言》和宪法之前，

sentences.en: Americans had the poSt.
sentences.zh: 美国人就已经有了邮政。

sentences.en: The underground Constitutional Post was crucial in fomenting the revolution,
sentences.zh: 地下的“宪政邮政”在煽动革命方面至关重要，

sentences.en: which gave America independence from England, but it was still a very limited system.
sentences.zh: 它让美国脱离了英国独立，但它仍然是一个非常有限的系统。

sentences.en: There were fewer than 100 post offices in the entire country,
sentences.zh: 全国只有不到100个邮局，

sentences.en: and the system didn't serve that many people,
sentences.zh: 这个系统服务的人群并不多，

sentences.en: and was basically a tool for political elites to communicate with each other.
sentences.zh: 基本上只是政治精英们相互交流的工具。

sentences.en: The founders wanted a better post,
sentences.zh: 开国元勋们想要一个更好的邮政系统，

sentences.en: one that would serve all people in their infant nation,
sentences.zh: 一个能服务于这个新生国家所有人民的系统，

sentences.en: and help them stay united under one flag.
sentences.zh: 并帮助他们在同一面旗帜下保持团结。

sentences.en: These people who were already spreading over the Appalachians into the wild west of Ohio and Kentucky.
sentences.zh: 这些人已经越过阿巴拉契亚山脉，进入了俄亥俄和肯塔基的荒野西部。

sentences.en: Founding father Benjamin Rush especially believed that the post office would play a crucial role
sentences.zh: 开国元勋本杰明·拉什特别相信邮政系统将在

sentences.en: in the new democracy.
sentences.zh: 新民主国家中发挥关键作用。

sentences.en: He was obsessed with the idea that the post office should circulate newspapers to every American.
sentences.zh: 他痴迷于邮政系统应该向每一位美国人分发报纸的想法。

sentences.en: You couldn't have an educated electorate if the people weren't literate,
sentences.zh: 如果人民没有受过教育，就不可能拥有受过教育的选民，

sentences.en: and they didn't have up-to-date political information.
sentences.zh: 而且他们也无法获得最新的政治信息。

sentences.en: But this would be no small undertaking.
sentences.zh: 但这绝非易事。

sentences.en: They'd need an infrastructure, a roads, and a workforce.
sentences.zh: 他们需要基础设施、道路和劳动力。

sentences.en: This government had very little money.
sentences.zh: 当时的政府几乎没有钱。

sentences.en: It was running on fumes.
sentences.zh: 它几乎是在勉强维持。

sentences.en: And yet he says, we're going to have this very, very ambitious postal system,
sentences.zh: 然而他说，我们要建立这个非常、非常雄心勃勃的邮政系统，

sentences.en: much more ambitious than anything in Europe.
sentences.zh: 比欧洲任何系统都要雄心勃勃。

sentences.en: It's really kind of astounding.
sentences.zh: 这真的很令人震惊。

sentences.en: In 1792, Congress passed the Post Office Act.
sentences.zh: 1792年，国会通过了《邮政法案》。

sentences.en: Under the Act, new postal routes were established.
sentences.zh: 根据该法案，建立了新的邮政路线。

sentences.en: Censoring or stealing mail became a punishable offense,
sentences.zh: 审查或窃取邮件成为可惩处的罪行，

sentences.en: and all newspapers could be mailed at the same low rate to promote the spread of information.
sentences.zh: 所有报纸都可以以同样的低费率邮寄，以促进信息传播。

sentences.en: It set off a huge explosion of newspapers from all sorts of political viewpoints.
sentences.zh: 这引发了各种政治观点的报纸的大爆发。

sentences.en: The post office was the main way, sometimes the only way, people got information.
sentences.zh: 邮政系统是人们获取信息的主要方式，有时甚至是唯一方式。

sentences.en: It was the media.
sentences.zh: 它就是当时的媒体。

sentences.en: We were news junkies back then.
sentences.zh: 那时我们都是新闻迷。

sentences.en: The founders ensured that we would have an uncensored, lively, contentious political culture,
sentences.zh: 开国元勋们确保了我们将拥有一个未经审查、充满活力、充满争议的政治文化，

sentences.en: because they wanted the people to be exposed to all kinds of views and argue it out and then vote.
sentences.zh: 因为他们希望人民接触到各种观点，进行辩论，然后投票。

sentences.en: We've been arguing and gossiping and spreading information, not all of it true, since the very beginning.
sentences.zh: 从一开始，我们就一直在争论、传播流言和信息，尽管并非所有信息都是真实的。

sentences.en: In a way, you know, you could take the attitude of they sort of created a Frankenstein,
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，你知道，你可以认为他们创造了一个“科学怪人”，

sentences.en: but in fact, it was by design.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，这是有意为之的。

sentences.en: Around this same time, in the late 1700s, the stagecoach was becoming a more popular way to travel
sentences.zh: 大约在同一时期，即18世纪末，驿站马车成为了一种更流行的旅行方式，

sentences.en: and a better way to carry mail than just packing up a rider on a horse.
sentences.zh: 也是比单纯让骑手骑马送信更好的邮件运输方式。

sentences.en: The post office started to contract with private stagecoach companies to carry mail,
sentences.zh: 邮政局开始与私人驿站马车公司签订合同来运送邮件，

sentences.en: and these companies worked with cities and towns to build roads.
sentences.zh: 这些公司与城镇合作修建道路。

sentences.en: In this way, the post helped carve out the early transportation infrastructure of the country,
sentences.zh: 通过这种方式，邮政帮助开辟了国家早期的交通基础设施，

sentences.en: connecting disparate communities.
sentences.zh: 连接了分散的社区。

sentences.en: When a group of people settled in a new place, the residents would petition the government for a post office,
sentences.zh: 当一群人定居在一个新地方时，居民们会向政府申请设立邮局，

sentences.en: which gave them an address and a place on the map.
sentences.zh: 这给了他们一个地址和地图上的位置。

sentences.en: And then that town would be connected to another town down the road.
sentences.zh: 然后那个城镇就会与路上的另一个城镇连接起来。

sentences.en: You started to have this kind of network.
sentences.zh: 你开始拥有了这种网络。

sentences.en: It's developed not just our physical landscape with roads, but a social landscape,
sentences.zh: 它不仅发展了我们的物理景观（道路），还发展了社会景观，

sentences.en: so that you could start to talk about this huge country with, like, some locations.
sentences.zh: 这样你就可以开始谈论这个巨大的国家，并带有一些具体的地点。

sentences.en: In 1831, when the French diplomat and writer Alexis de Tocqueville toured America,
sentences.zh: 1831年，当法国外交官兼作家亚历克西·德·托克维尔游历美国时，

sentences.en: he was amazed by our postal system.
sentences.zh: 他被我们的邮政系统惊呆了。

sentences.en: He's riding in a stagecoach through someplace in the Michigan outback,
sentences.zh: 他坐着驿站马车穿过密歇根内陆的某个地方，

sentences.en: and he sees people coming out of these kind of crude huts, you know, cabins,
sentences.zh: 他看到人们从那些简陋的小屋里走出来，

sentences.en: desperate to get the newspapers and able to talk about not just American politics,
sentences.zh: 渴望得到报纸，并且能够谈论不仅是美国政治，

sentences.en: but what's going on in Europe.
sentences.zh: 还有欧洲正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: He's flabbergasted.
sentences.zh: 他惊呆了。

sentences.en: At this point, the mail in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在这一点上，美国的邮件

sentences.en: was mostly about sending and receiving newspapers.
sentences.zh: 主要是关于发送和接收报纸。

sentences.en: People didn't really send letters because they couldn't afford to.
sentences.zh: 人们并不真正寄信，因为他们负担不起。

sentences.en: They kept the rates for letters high, and they used that revenue from letters
sentences.zh: 他们保持高昂的信件邮费，并利用信件收入

sentences.en: to pay for the delivery of newspapers to all Americans everywhere.
sentences.zh: 来支付向所有美国人投递报纸的费用。

sentences.en: Most people got, like, fewer than one letter a year.
sentences.zh: 大多数人一年收到的信件不到一封。

sentences.en: You'd get a letter saying, you know, Pa has died, or you'd get, like, Aunt Letitia's will.
sentences.zh: 你会收到一封信说，你知道，父亲去世了，或者你会收到莱蒂西亚姑妈的遗嘱。

sentences.en: And unlike today, where the person sending a letter covers the cost of postage,
sentences.zh: 而且与今天寄信人支付邮费不同，

sentences.en: back then, the recipient had to pay.
sentences.zh: 当时是由收件人付费。

sentences.en: You'd go to the post office, you'd stand in line and see if you had mail,
sentences.zh: 你会去邮局，排队看看是否有你的邮件，

sentences.en: and then pay for it if you wanted it.
sentences.zh: 如果你想要的话，就付钱。

sentences.en: It created this fantastic backlog of unclaimed mail because so many people,
sentences.zh: 这造成了大量无人认领邮件的积压，因为很多人，

sentences.en: so many people didn't want to pay.
sentences.zh: 很多人不想付钱。

sentences.en: In the 1840s and 50s, the population of the country exploded with new immigrants,
sentences.zh: 在19世纪40和50年代，随着新移民的涌入，国家人口激增，

sentences.en: and all these new people wanted a less expensive way to communicate.
sentences.zh: 所有这些新移民都想要一种更便宜的交流方式。

sentences.en: A movement for cheap postage started to form.
sentences.zh: 一场关于廉价邮资的运动开始形成。

sentences.en: This movement wanted people to be able to send letters anywhere in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这场运动希望人们能够以一个低廉的价格，

sentences.en: for one low price, using a new tool, the prepaid postage stamp.
sentences.zh: 使用一种新工具——预付邮资的邮票，向美国任何地方寄信。

sentences.en: They argued that the volume of the mail would increase to a degree
sentences.zh: 他们认为邮件量会增加到一定程度，

sentences.en: that would make up for the revenue, and they were correct,
sentences.zh: 足以弥补收入损失，他们是对的，

sentences.en: because the volume of the mail really went gangbusters after cheap postage.
sentences.zh: 因为在廉价邮资之后，邮件量确实猛增了。

sentences.en: The postage stamp allowed regular people to send letters.
sentences.zh: 邮票让普通人也能寄信。

sentences.en: People sent enough letters to fill thousands of Ken Burns documentaries.
sentences.zh: 人们寄出的信件足以填满成千上万部肯·伯恩斯的纪录片。

sentences.en: It was the Victorian era, and letter writing became an art form.
sentences.zh: 那是维多利亚时代，写信成为了一种艺术形式。

sentences.en: There were even books with advice on how to refine your letter writing style.
sentences.zh: 甚至还有专门的书籍，提供如何提升书信写作风格的建议。

sentences.en: Address your correspondent by his or her title, not the first name.
sentences.zh: 称呼收信人时要用头衔，而不是名字。

sentences.en: Dear husband, beloved brother, dearest friend, honored sir.
sentences.zh: 亲爱的丈夫、敬爱的兄弟、最亲爱的朋友、尊敬的先生。

sentences.en: No matter how close you are, don't address him by his first name.
sentences.zh: 无论你们关系有多亲密，都不要直呼其名。

sentences.en: Begin your letter with, I take pen in hand.
sentences.zh: 信的开头要写：我提笔写道。

sentences.en: Please pardon the poor paper, the scratchy pen, the ungraceful language.
sentences.zh: 请原谅这粗糙的纸张、难用的钢笔和笨拙的语言。

sentences.en: Women especially became avid letter writers.
sentences.zh: 女性尤其成为了狂热的写信者。

sentences.en: Women actually started wearing little lockets around their necks with their stamps inside.
sentences.zh: 女性甚至开始在脖子上戴小挂坠，里面装着邮票。

sentences.en: With more women using the post office, the place itself began to change.
sentences.zh: 随着越来越多的女性使用邮局，邮局本身也开始发生变化。

sentences.en: Post offices historically had been often in the backs of taverns.
sentences.zh: 历史上，邮局通常设在酒馆的后方。

sentences.en: They were men's social spaces.
sentences.zh: 那是男性的社交场所。

sentences.en: You know, there were prostitutes at the post office supplying their wares and pickpock, famously pickpockets.
sentences.zh: 你知道，邮局里曾有妓女兜售生意，还有臭名昭著的扒手。

sentences.en: When women started sending letters, post offices added special ladies' windows so that ladies could pick up their letters without coming into contact with these unseemly elements.
sentences.zh: 当女性开始寄信时，邮局增设了专门的女士窗口，这样女士们就可以在不接触这些不体面的人的情况下领取信件。

sentences.en: Slowly, post offices transitioned into more professional spaces.
sentences.zh: 慢慢地，邮局转型成了更专业的场所。

sentences.en: By 1860, there were some 28,000 post offices in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 到1860年，美国大约有28000个邮局。

sentences.en: People were sending thousands of letters and newly invented greeting cards to each other.
sentences.zh: 人们互相寄送成千上万封信件和新发明的贺卡。

sentences.en: But they were also using the post, just like the founders intended, to disseminate political information.
sentences.zh: 但他们也像创始人所预想的那样，利用邮政系统传播政治信息。

sentences.en: Abolitionists, for example, were using the mail to spread ideas about ending slavery.
sentences.zh: 例如，废奴主义者利用邮件传播关于终结奴隶制的思想。

sentences.en: In the 1860s, when the Civil War was being fought over some of those very ideas,
sentences.zh: 在19世纪60年代，当内战因其中一些思想而爆发时，

sentences.en: the American post office would bifurcate for a time.
sentences.zh: 美国邮政系统曾一度分裂。

sentences.en: No mail would be sent between North and South.
sentences.zh: 南北之间不再有邮件往来。

sentences.en: And the Civil War brought another big change in America's postal system.
sentences.zh: 内战也给美国的邮政系统带来了另一个重大变革。

sentences.en: Home delivery.
sentences.zh: 送货上门。

sentences.en: A postal employee in Ohio named Joseph Briggs found it heartbreaking during the war
sentences.zh: 俄亥俄州一位名叫约瑟夫·布里格斯的邮政员工在战争期间感到非常心碎，

sentences.en: because people desperate for news of their soldiers away would have to stand in long lines at the post office.
sentences.zh: 因为那些急切想得到远方士兵消息的人们不得不排长队在邮局等候。

sentences.en: Often these people would be receiving news of a loved one's death.
sentences.zh: 这些人往往会收到亲人去世的消息。

sentences.en: And there were just scenes of terrible, terrible grief in public.
sentences.zh: 公共场合里到处都是极其悲痛的场景。

sentences.en: They didn't even have privacy.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至没有隐私可言。

sentences.en: And he found it so heartbreaking that he ran this pilot program of bringing people the mail.
sentences.zh: 他觉得这太令人心碎了，于是开展了一个为人们送邮件上门的试点项目。

sentences.en: Home delivery caught on, and by the mid-1860s, many cities were offering it.
sentences.zh: 送货上门服务流行了起来，到19世纪60年代中期，许多城市都提供了这项服务。

sentences.en: About 30 years later, people living in rural areas would also get home delivery.
sentences.zh: 大约30年后，居住在农村地区的人们也能享受到送货上门服务。

sentences.en: But while people in the eastern United States entered a letter-writing boom,
sentences.zh: 但就在美国东部地区掀起写信热潮的同时，

sentences.en: news settlers in California felt isolated.
sentences.zh: 加利福尼亚的新定居者却感到与世隔绝。

sentences.en: It was hard to receive mail on the West CoaSt.
sentences.zh: 在西海岸收信非常困难。

sentences.en: So the mail could go by train to Missouri,
sentences.zh: 邮件可以先通过火车运到密苏里州，

sentences.en: but then it had to be hauled by stagecoaches through really terrible conditions.
sentences.zh: 但之后必须由驿站马车在极其恶劣的条件下运送。

sentences.en: The other option would be to send a letter on a 13,000-mile six-month trip
sentences.zh: 另一个选择是让信件经历一段13000英里、为期六个月的旅程，

sentences.en: around the tip of South America by boat.
sentences.zh: 乘船绕过南美洲南端。

sentences.en: Californians, as they became more powerful by the Gold Rush era and the succeeding years,
sentences.zh: 随着淘金热时期及随后的几年里加州人变得越来越有势力，

sentences.en: became outraged by the fact that they had this lousy postal service.
sentences.zh: 他们对这种糟糕的邮政服务感到愤怒。

sentences.en: And they demanded to have a reliable stagecoach mail that would depart and arrive on predictable times.
sentences.zh: 他们要求建立一种可靠的驿站马车邮政，能够按预定时间出发和到达。

sentences.en: Eventually, they got what they wanted.
sentences.zh: 最终，他们如愿以偿。

sentences.en: By 1857, the post office had a fairly reliable route from east to weSt.
sentences.zh: 到1857年，邮局已经拥有了一条相当可靠的从东到西的路线。

sentences.en: It took 25 days, which was better than it had been, but it was still not great.
sentences.zh: 全程需要25天，这比以前好多了，但仍然不够理想。

sentences.en: A group of businessmen led by a guy named William Russell
sentences.zh: 一群由威廉·拉塞尔领导的商人，

sentences.en: thought that they could do better than the U.S.
sentences.zh: 认为他们可以比美国邮政做得更好。

sentences.en: PoSt.
sentences.zh: 邮政。

sentences.en: Russell thought his little startup company could get the mail from St. Joseph, Missouri
sentences.zh: 拉塞尔认为他的小型初创公司可以在短短10天内将邮件从密苏里州的圣约瑟夫

sentences.en: to Sacramento, California in just 10 days.
sentences.zh: 送到加利福尼亚州的萨克拉门托。

sentences.en: In fact, he did it.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他做到了。

sentences.en: People didn't think he'd be able to do it.
sentences.zh: 人们原本认为他做不到。

sentences.en: Russell's competing service was called the Pony Express.
sentences.zh: 拉塞尔的竞争服务被称为“小马快递”。

sentences.en: Riders on horseback would race at full speed for about 10 or 15 miles to relay stations
sentences.zh: 骑手们会骑马全速奔跑约10到15英里到达中转站，

sentences.en: where they would trade out for a rested horse.
sentences.zh: 在那里换上一匹休息好的马。

sentences.en: This change was supposed to take only two minutes.
sentences.zh: 这个更换过程只需要两分钟。

sentences.en: Horses were to carry no more than 165 pounds, including the rider.
sentences.zh: 马匹负重不得超过165磅，包括骑手在内。

sentences.en: If an exhausted horse collapsed on the trail,
sentences.zh: 如果一匹精疲力竭的马在途中倒下，

sentences.en: the rider was to run on foot to the next location with his bag of mail.
sentences.zh: 骑手必须背着邮包徒步跑到下一个地点。

sentences.en: It was a very expensive endeavor, and it didn't last long, about a year and a half.
sentences.zh: 这是一项非常昂贵的工程，而且持续时间不长，大约只有一年半。

sentences.en: Which was okay, because by 1861,
sentences.zh: 但这也没关系，因为到了1861年，

sentences.en: the Transcontinental Telegraph would reach California,
sentences.zh: 横贯大陆的电报线将抵达加利福尼亚，

sentences.en: and rail service would soon follow.
sentences.zh: 铁路服务也将随之而来。

sentences.en: Trains would eventually deliver mail all over the U.S.,
sentences.zh: 火车最终将把邮件送到美国各地，

sentences.en: and not just deliver it, but become moving post offices.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是运送，它们还成为了移动的邮局。

sentences.en: In fact, subsidies from the post office allowed the rail system to expand throughout the country.
sentences.zh: 事实上，来自邮局的补贴使铁路系统得以在全国范围内扩张。

sentences.en: Trains couldn't afford to run on passenger fare alone.
sentences.zh: 火车仅靠客运票价是无法维持运营的。

sentences.en: The money they got from the post office was crucial in helping them expand service.
sentences.zh: 他们从邮局获得的资金对于帮助他们扩大服务至关重要。

sentences.en: Years earlier, these postal subsidies had done the same thing for stagecoaches,
sentences.zh: 多年前，这些邮政补贴也曾为驿站马车做过同样的事情，

sentences.en: and after World War I, the posts would do this again for aviation.
sentences.zh: 而在第一次世界大战后，邮政系统又为航空业做了同样的事。

sentences.en: Planes were not a viable form of transportation
sentences.zh: 飞机并不是一种可行的交通工具，

sentences.en: until the post office poured money into the industry.
sentences.zh: 直到邮局向该行业投入了大量资金。

sentences.en: The aviation industry wasn't able to pay for itself with passenger service
sentences.zh: 航空业直到20世纪40年代后期，

sentences.en: until well into the 1940s.
sentences.zh: 才能够通过客运服务实现自给自足。

sentences.en: The industry survived and expanded by carrying mail for the post office.
sentences.zh: 该行业通过为邮局运送邮件得以生存和扩张。

sentences.en: In fact, before Charles Lindbergh made his historic nonstop flight across the Atlantic,
sentences.zh: 事实上，在查尔斯·林德伯格完成那次历史性的横跨大西洋不着陆飞行之前，

sentences.en: he had another job.
sentences.zh: 他还有另一份工作。

sentences.en: Charles Lindbergh was a night pilot.
sentences.zh: 查尔斯·林德伯格曾是一名夜间飞行员。

sentences.en: You know, he carried the mail.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他负责运送邮件。

sentences.en: If the post office truly created America,
sentences.zh: 如果说邮局真正创造了美国，

sentences.en: and I think Winifred Gallagher makes a pretty good case that it did,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为温妮弗雷德·加拉格尔提出的论点非常有说服力，

sentences.en: it's now playing a more supporting role.
sentences.zh: 那么它现在正扮演着更辅助的角色。

sentences.en: In the last 40 years or so, Congress has cut back considerably on services.
sentences.zh: 在过去40年左右的时间里，国会大幅削减了服务。

sentences.en: And if you've noticed longer lines at the post office
sentences.zh: 如果你注意到邮局排队的时间变长了，

sentences.en: and delays in receiving your mail, that's why.
sentences.zh: 或者收信出现了延误，原因就在这里。

sentences.en: In my opinion, no one should be mad at the post office.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，没有人应该对邮局感到愤怒。

sentences.en: They should be mad at Congress.
sentences.zh: 他们应该对国会感到愤怒。

sentences.en: Congress has prevented the post office from modernizing and running itself efficiently
sentences.zh: 国会阻碍了邮局的现代化和高效运营，

sentences.en: and tragically going digital, which it should have done back in the 80s.
sentences.zh: 也阻碍了它本应在80年代就进行的数字化转型。

sentences.en: Gallagher believes the post office missed an opportunity to facilitate email
sentences.zh: 加拉格尔认为邮局错失了促进电子邮件

sentences.en: and other digital communication.
sentences.zh: 和其他数字通信发展的机会。

sentences.en: But she argues the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但她认为美国邮政署，

sentences.en: Postal Service probably isn't on the brink of death either.
sentences.zh: 可能并没有濒临倒闭。

sentences.en: Conservatives talk about privatizing the whole operation,
sentences.zh: 保守派谈论着将整个业务私有化，

sentences.en: but right now, Gallagher doubts that this is possible.
sentences.zh: 但目前，加拉格尔怀疑这是否可行。

sentences.en: Actually, the private competitors, neither FedEx or UPS is equipped
sentences.zh: 事实上，私人竞争对手，无论是联邦快递还是联合包裹服务公司，都没有能力

sentences.en: to handle the volume of American mail.
sentences.zh: 处理美国邮件的业务量。

sentences.en: They would certainly risk bankruptcy if they tried.
sentences.zh: 如果他们尝试这样做，肯定会面临破产的风险。

sentences.en: The post office has an unparalleled delivery infrastructure
sentences.zh: 邮局拥有无与伦比的投递基础设施，

sentences.en: and employs an enormous workforce.
sentences.zh: 并雇佣了庞大的员工队伍。

sentences.en: And we still need the service they provide.
sentences.zh: 而且我们仍然需要他们提供的服务。

sentences.en: Because unlike FedEx and UPS,
sentences.zh: 因为与联邦快递和联合包裹不同，

sentences.en: the U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国邮政署，

sentences.en: Post Office cannot pick and choose where they deliver based on profit.
sentences.zh: 不能根据利润来选择投递地点。

sentences.en: It is obliged, by law, to provide pickups and deliveries to every community in the country,
sentences.zh: 法律规定，它必须为全国每一个社区提供收件和投递服务，

sentences.en: even if that community is located in the bottom of the Grand Canyon.
sentences.zh: 即使那个社区位于大峡谷的底部。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Katie Mengel,
sentences.zh: 本周的《99%隐形》节目由凯蒂·门格尔制作，

sentences.en: with Delaney Hall, Sharif Youssef, Avery Truffleman,
sentences.zh: 参与制作的还有德莱尼·霍尔、谢里夫·优素福、艾弗里·特鲁夫曼，

sentences.en: Emmett Fitzgerald, Sam Greenspan, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 埃米特·菲茨杰拉德、萨姆·格林斯潘，以及我，罗曼·马斯。

sentences.en: Kurt Kolstad is our digital director.
sentences.zh: 库尔特·科尔斯塔德是我们的数字总监。

sentences.en: Taryn Mazza takes care of the office, and us all.
sentences.zh: 塔琳·马扎负责办公室事务，也照顾我们所有人。

sentences.en: Sean Rial composed all the music.
sentences.zh: 肖恩·里亚尔负责创作了所有的音乐。

sentences.en: And Michelle Loeffler knows a lot about the post office.
sentences.zh: 米歇尔·洛弗勒对邮局了解颇深。

sentences.en: We are a project of 91.7 KALW in San Francisco,
sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山91.7 KALW电台的一个项目，

sentences.en: and produced on Radio Row in beautiful downtown Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 在加利福尼亚州奥克兰市中心美丽的“广播街”制作。

sentences.en: You can find the show and join discussions about the show on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 你可以在Facebook上找到我们的节目并参与讨论。

sentences.en: You can tweet at me, at Roman Mars, and the show at 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 你可以在推特上关注我，@RomanMars，也可以关注节目官网99pi.org。

sentences.en: We're on Instagram and Tumblr, too.
sentences.zh: 我们也在Instagram和Tumblr上。

sentences.en: But if you want to read a story about the British Navy building an unsinkable ship
sentences.zh: 但如果你想读一个关于英国海军建造一艘不沉之舰的故事，

sentences.en: made of ice and wood pulp instead of steel,
sentences.zh: 那艘船是用冰和木浆而不是钢材制成的，

sentences.en: that's a real thing,
sentences.zh: 那是真实发生过的事情，

sentences.en: you have to go to 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 你必须访问99pi.org。

sentences.en: Radiotopia.
sentences.zh: Radiotopia。
